value.body: A type rating is an endorsement on a pilot's licence that allows them to fly a specific aircraft type, such as the Airbus A320 or Boeing 737. It is needed on top of a Commercial Pilot Licence (CPL) to fly airliners as a first officer, and involves ground school, simulator training and a skill test, with endorsement by DGCA.

items.label: Prerequisite
items.note: With instrument rating and a current medical

items.label: Training
items.note: Then a skill test and DGCA endorsement

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A DGCA-issued or validated CPL. The type rating is taken either self-sponsored at an approved training organisation, or through an airline's cadet or new-hire programme, where the airline arranges the training — often with a service bond or cost-recovery terms.

value.title: At a glance
items: A self-sponsored type rating does not guarantee a job; airlines still run their own selection.
Ratings need recent flying to stay current, so a long gap before a job can mean extra training costs.
Airline-arranged training lowers the upfront cost but usually ties you to that airline for a period.
The type you choose limits you to airlines that fly it.
